OrderPlus SQM · Supply & Quality Manager

Blueprint UX/UI & Design System v2

The current state with real screenshots, the full Design System v2, 35 new UI screens (desktop & mobile) and a prompt pack for creating the draft on Lovable. Focus: the QC module used on phones in kitchens, warehouses and factories.

Directional reference: the new designs are a direction; real implementation may differ and be more accurate.

★Executive summary

One document with four parts: (A) the current state with real screenshots, (B) the full Design System v2, (C) 35 new UI screens built from that same Design System at desktop and mobile, and (D) a prompt pack for creating the draft on Lovable.

new screens, each with a 1440px desktop and a 390px mobile version

The three decisions that matter most

P0 Bugs that corrupt QC data

Creating a category fails silently (F-01), “fake completion” when a required field is empty (F-02), a raw technical error banner (F-03). These need fixing before any polish; screens and rules R-10 → R-15 are already in place.

P1 QC on a phone is not usable in the field yet

Almost a full screen sits in front of the first item, the tick box is ~24px, the “Next item” button floats in the content, and offline behaviour is unclear. v2 uses “field” density (48px), one row per item, a bottom-sticky action bar and camera-first capture.

P1 The design system is incomplete, not wrong

Brand colours and breakpoints are on standard. Missing: density, mobile patterns, save state, a semantic status table, AA contrast. v2 adds exactly those and keeps the brand identity.

Major changes in Design System v2

  • Keep navy #0050A0 · teal #00A096 · red #E8000C · Noto Sans · radius · navy-tint elevation · breakpoints.
  • Add teal-600, green-600, orange-600, gray-650 so white text/secondary text reach WCAG AA.
  • Add 3 densities (compact · comfortable · field), 3 app-shell forms (Sidebar · Rail · BottomNav), container-query layout.
  • Add 20 new/standardised component groups: PageHeader, FilterBar, DataView (table↔rows), StatusBadge, SaveState, StickyActionBar, ResponsiveDialog, QuantityInput, ChecklistItem, Camera…
  • Add 36 R-xx rules, each traced back to a finding F-xx and with a way to verify it.

Quick reading guide

You want to…Read
See the real current stateA3 (screenshots) → A4 (findings register)
Understand why and what was designedA6 (design-system analysis) → B1 (rules) → B2–B3
See the new interfacePart C: each screen has a “Current ↔ New design” tab (desktop) and the old mobile image next to the new mobile
Take it to LovableD1 (how to use) → D2 (prompts P0–P7) → D3 (data impact) → D4–D5 (map, acceptance)
How the mockups are builtEvery Part C screen is generated with exactly the CSS and components from Part B — nothing is hand-drawn. Each screen uses one HTML fragment, displayed at 1440px and 390px thanks to container queries, so the desktop/mobile difference is the Design System’s responsive behaviour rather than two separate designs.
A note about the new designsThe new designs in this document (Part C and the samples in Part B) are a directional reference for UX/UI, not a final specification. Some details may not be exactly right — layout, sizes, sample content, on-screen text, behaviour. Real implementation may differ, and will be more accurate after testing with real users, real data and technical constraints. When a mockup conflicts with an R-xx rule or with real data, prefer the rule and the data, then note the difference.
What could not be confirmedMobile screenshots were taken at a 606px viewport (wider than a real phone). The Lovable code is older than production. Offline/queue behaviour and the data source for the “QC Report” need engineering confirmation — see D3 and D6.
Part A

Current state

Real screenshots, the findings register and an analysis of the running design system.

A1Scope & method

This report records the current state of orderplusscm.vercel.app (OrderPlus Supply & Quality Manager) exactly as observed on 18–19 Sep 2026, as the basis for Design System v2 in Part B and the new screens in Part C.

SourceHow it was doneUsed for
Production (workspace “tested”)The user’s own signed-in Chrome; captured 26 desktop screenshots (1486×812) and 21 mobile screenshots (606 CSS px viewport, 952×1277 images) — every image in this document is a real screenshot, not a re-creation.Visual evidence and real measurements (tick box, row height, contents length).
Real actions in QCTicked complete, picked a dropdown, typed a [HungTest] note, tried to create a QC category twice.Findings F-01 → F-05 (reproduced errors, not guesses).
Lovable project orderplusscmRead the source: pages, components/qc, lib/qc (qcApi, qcValidation), index.css, Supabase migrations, edge functions.QC data model, completion/late rules, tokens; note this code is older than production (F-33).
Brand Guidelines v1.1 · Style HubThe Tokens/Components pages of orderplus-sqm-bg.lovable.app.The source of truth for colour, type, radius, elevation, breakpoints.

Limitations to be aware of

  • Mobile screenshots were taken at a 606px viewport (a window-tool limit), wider than a real phone (360–414px) — the layout problems here are likely worse on a real device, not milder. The new mockups in Part C are built at 390px.
  • The screenshots show the Vietnamese production UI; UI labels quoted in this English version of the document are translated into English.
  • The login screen has no real screenshot (it was only observed in the first session); the new screen is built from the i18n strings already seen.
  • Real emails/names in the User management and Profile screenshots have been blurred.
  • Test data created: the item “Check staff health & hygiene clothing” (branch Alexidntest, 2026-09-18) — ticked complete, Hygiene status = pass, note starting with [HungTest]. It can be reverted to “not started” when needed.
  • Items marked “read from code” (source code in the findings register) were not verified directly on production.

Main user groups & devices

RoleDevice & contextMain tasksDesign priority
Branch QC staffPhone, standing, one hand; kitchen/warehouse/factory; gloves, harsh light, weak network, frequent interruptionsDo shift checklists, capture evidence, report issuesMobile-first · “field” density · autosave · offline
Branch managerPhone + tablet; moving between kitchen and officeTrack shift progress, handle corrective actions, approveMobile + tablet · quick overview
QA / Headquarters (HQ)Desktop computer, seated in an officeAuthor the standard QC Manual, push it to branches, read trend reportsDesktop · compact/comfortable density
StorekeeperPhone/tablet in the warehouse; sometimes a computerReceive/issue/transfer, stock count, adjustmentsMobile · fast number entry · posting with confirmation
System administratorDesktop computerOrganizations, users, permissions, locations, languagesDesktop · dangerous actions are protected

A4Findings register

34 findings: 3 P0 (blocking/data risk), 12 P1 (major impact), 19 P2 (improvement). The “Recommendation” column points to a rule (R-xx) in section B1 or a component in B3, and to the fixing screen in Part C.

IDLevelAreaFindingEvidenceImpactRecommendation (rule · component · screen)
F-01P0QCCreating a QC Category fails silentlyTap Add category → type a name → Save: the dialog closes as if it succeeded, no error toast, and the “Categories” count is still 5 after a reload. Reproduced 2 out of 2 times.
Images: desktop · qc-add-category
Managers believe they created an inspection standard but nothing was written; setting up checklists is completely blocked.R-11 (never fail silently) · Dialog stays open when saving fails · screen qc-add-category
F-02P0QC“Complete” is separate from required fields → fake completionTicking “Check completed” while the required field “Hygiene status *” is still empty: the system still records “Completed by Hung · 17:40 KST”.
Images: desktop · qc-item-expanded · mobile · qc-checklist-items
The QC report can show 100% even though required hygiene/food-safety data was never entered — a compliance and audit-trail risk.R-12 (complete = every required field valid) · ChecklistItem/CompleteButton · screen qc-item
F-03P0QCRaw configuration error banner, mixing 3 languages, permanently visible“Configuration changes were not applied” followed by 8 verbatim lines “a field needs one name stored as written” for draft items (1, 2, test, suhu, shuh, Temper…); the same content repeats in a merged toast at the bottom right.
Images: desktop · qc-error-banner · mobile · qc-manuals
Backend messages leak into the branch manager’s UI and make the product look broken; the same error is reported in two places.R-13 (errors in plain language, reported in one place) · Item-level Notice + “Fix now” · screen qc-manuals
F-04P1QCThree different save behaviours on the same check itemTick = saves instantly; note = saves on blur; data fields = must press a separate “Submit”. One form shows both “Saved on the server” and “Saved on this device”.
Images: desktop · qc-item-expanded
Staff who are interrupted (a customer, an incoming call, the OS reclaiming the tab) can lose data without knowing.R-10 (one save model) · SaveState + useAutosave · screen qc-item

Images: desktop · qc-item-expanded

A5What to keep

Not everything needs to change. The following already work well and carry over into v2 unchanged.

Sidebar navy “control tower”

Two clear groups, the selected state is highlighted — true to the Brand Guidelines spirit. Kept on desktop; collapses into a rail (tablet) and a bottom nav (mobile).

The “Standard manual → push to branches” model

Separates the HQ standard from each branch’s copy, with a context banner. Keep it and make it clearer with a diff screen before pushing.

The “Next unchecked item” button

Solves exactly the problem of a 30-item checklist. Promote it to the primary bottom-sticky action on mobile.

Daily checklist snapshots

qc_get_or_create_records stores a snapshot of the category/item at the time of recording, so later edits to the standard do not corrupt history. Keep it unchanged when rebuilding the UI.

Client-side photo/video compression

Suits weak Wi‑Fi in kitchens/warehouses. Keep it; only split the steps “Compressing / Sending” and add Cancel.

Dynamic permissions

quality_control.manage / execute come from the role_permissions table and are configurable per organization. Keep.

Permissions on mobile

The matrix is already turned into a role picker + a permission list — standardise it as a pattern for every matrix table.

Compact mobile header

Menu · workspace · language · avatar on one row, does not break at 606px. It only needs to be consistent across pages.

Colour tokens & breakpoints match the guideline

navy-500 #0050A0, teal-500 #00A096, red #E8000C, breakpoint md = 768 are already correct.

Consistent Lucide icons

One single icon set with the same stroke weight. Keep.

A7QC module: business rules & data model

Understanding this model correctly is a precondition for rebuilding the UI without breaking the business logic. Summarised from qcApi.ts, qcValidation.ts, the migrations and actions on production.

Data model
  • quality_control (1 root per workspace) → qc_categories (categories, with sort_order) → qc_items (check items; preferred_time: opening / mid_day / closing / custom; is_required).
  • Each day × branch: the RPC qc_get_or_create_records generates qc_checklist_records, storing a snapshot of the category/item.
  • qc_calendar_summary feeds the monthly calendar.
  • Evidence lives in response_data (checkbox, text, images[], videos[], audios[], files[]); files sit in the qc-evidence bucket with a 1-hour signed URL; videos/files are auto-deleted after 31 days (edge function qc-evidence-cleanup).
Business rules
  • Completion (isResponseComplete): an item with a checkbox only needs the tick; photo/video/text are optional evidence. v2 proposal: complete only when every required field is valid (F-02).
  • Late (computeIsLate): opening after 11:00, mid_day after 15:00, closing is never late, custom = time + 2h; past days are always late.
  • Permissions: quality_control.manage (HQ/QA) is separate from quality_control.execute (branch), loaded dynamically from role_permissions.
  • Corrective actions: closed only when the re-check passes (a read-only screen).
Real data observed
  • Standard manual: 5 categories · 30 items · 23 required.
  • 개점 준비 (Opening) 7 · 조리 및 식품안전 6 · 영업 중 위생 5 (4 required) · 마감 점검 6 · 주간 정기 점검 6.
  • QC item content (name, instructions, field labels) is user-entered data, currently in Korean — kept as is and not translated; only system labels are multilingual.
  • Test branch: Alexidntest · workspace “tested · test”.
Today’s QC journey (mobile) → pain points
  1. Open QC Checklists → pass through the hero, branch picker, date, view mode F-06
  2. Tap “Next unchecked item” (floating in the flow) F-06
  3. Open an item → fill in fields (data type unclear) F-05
  4. Tick “complete” even though a required * field is empty F-02
  5. Press a separate Submit; notes save on blur F-04
  6. Capture a photo through the file picker F-09
  7. Connection drops → unclear what happens F-08
A theme running through everythingThe system often stays silent when an action fails (F-01, F-03, F-04). For field QC staff this is more dangerous than a display bug: they will trust that the data was recorded when in fact it was not. Rules R-10 → R-14 in Part B come directly from here.
Part B

Design System v2

Principles, UX/UI rules, tokens, components, patterns, code and the migration map.

B1UX/UI principles & rules

Design System v2 keeps the brand identity (navy · teal · Noto Sans) and adds what Brand Guidelines v1.1 lacks: density, mobile patterns, save state, status semantics and contrast. The six principles below lead to 36 verifiable rules.

1 · The right job first, beauty second

QC users come to finish their shift, not to admire the interface. Every screen has one main job, placed where the thumb reaches.

2 · Never silent

Every action ends in one of three results: Saving, Saved, or Could not save with a way to recover. User data must never disappear.

3 · One pattern per job

One PageHeader, one filter bar, one table↔cards component, one status table, one save model. Learn once, use everywhere.

4 · Adapt to context

The same component has three densities (compact · comfortable · field) and changes layout with the width of its container, without duplicating the design.

5 · Readable in the worst places

Contrast ≥ 4.5:1, text ≥ 14px, touch targets ≥ 44px: designed for damp kitchens, dark storerooms, gloved hands and scratched screens.

6 · The user’s language

System labels come in all four languages (VI · EN · KO · ID), messages speak plainly, numbers/dates follow the locale. Content that users type themselves (UGC) stays as typed and needs no translation.

36 UX/UI rules (R-xx)

Every rule has a reason (linking to a finding F-xx) and a way to verify it; use them as acceptance criteria in the Lovable pack (Part D).

Layout & navigation
R-01
Every page uses one PageHeader: breadcrumb (desktop) · title · one-line description · at most 1 primary action. There is only one back button: in the Topbar on mobile — the PageHeader does not repeat it.Users know at once “what page is this, what do I do next” on every page (F-10).Verify: No more gradient hero, icon tile, workspace chip or a second “Back” button at the top of a page.
R-04
Below 768px, tables become a list of flat record rows; a table must never scroll horizontally on mobile. Secondary navigation (contents, long tabs) collapses or becomes a picker.A record can be read at a glance (F-13, F-15).Verify: Open the page at 390px: no horizontal scrollbar and no wrapped column headers.
R-09
The filter bar has 1 search field + at most 3 visible filters; the rest go into a “Filters (n)” sheet. Active filters show as removable chips.Data must appear on the first screen (F-14).Verify: On mobile, the list starts within 400px of the top of the page.
R-26
Workspace/organization context lives only in the Topbar (the avatar menu on mobile). Do not repeat a workspace chip in the page header.A single place to switch and see the context (F-26).Verify: Search the page content for “tested · test”: none.
R-31
Forms and detail pages use Sections (title + description + spacing, separated by a hairline), not a box around every field group. A Card is only for a standalone object: a record, a KPI, a summary panel. Never nest a box inside a box.Saves horizontal/vertical space (especially at 390px) and reduces visual noise; content is not squeezed by 2–3 layers of padding.Verify: Measure the margin from the screen edge to the text: ≤ 16px for form content.
R-32
On mobile, one field per row; pair fields only when both are short values (country code + phone number, quantity + unit). Fields have short labels and placeholders that fit the width; help text sits below the field and does not misalign rows.Placeholders are not clipped; the layout does not skew depending on whether a field has a note (extends F-13).Verify: At 390px: no clipped placeholders/labels and the fields line up.
R-33
Mobile Topbar: root pages show the module name; sub-pages show “‹ parent name”. The Topbar title never repeats the page H1; there is no dedicated menu button (primary navigation lives in the bottom bar and the “More” menu — R-35).A single way back, no repeated title (F-25).Verify: Each sub-page: exactly one back chevron; the title appears only once on the first screen.
R-34
On mobile, content is flat by default: lists are rows separated by hairlines (no border around each row), stat groups are one divided strip, and calendars/charts/forms sit directly on the page background. Use a box only when the content needs a container: Notice, Dialog/Sheet, tappable tiles, the QC progress band. Choose using the “Container policy” table in B4.Every layer of border + padding takes ~30px of width (≈9% of a 390px screen); a 7-column calendar benefits most. It also avoids many repeated boxes cluttering the view.Verify: At 390px: content width ≥ 358px (16 + 16 margins), calendar cells ≥ 46px, no box around lists.
R-35
Mobile navigation has two tiers: a fixed bottom bar (the highest-level destinations, identical on every screen) and module tabs under the Topbar (the sub-pages of the open module). If the user can reach only one module, its sub-pages move up to the bottom bar. The bar shows only the modules the user has permission for, in a fixed order (the “Permission → bottom bar” table in B4). The selected item is always the module that contains the current page; deep pages have a ‹ parent button; task pages hide the bottom bar and keep only the StickyActionBar.Users always know where they are and how to go on; there are no two different bottom bars and no “More” that means several things (F-25).Verify: Walk through every screen: the bottom bar never changes its content; each page has exactly one lit item; each deep page has exactly one back button.
R-36
Every row-type component (ListItem, RecordRow, ChecklistItem) must withstand long text and narrow containers: a text area ≥ ~144px, the trailing element drops under the title when there is not enough room, codes never break mid-token. Test with the “3 widths × short/long title” check before it enters the library.Real data has long names (Vietnamese, Korean, dish names); a component that only looks good with short data is not finished (F-13).Verify: Open the ListItem specimen at 260/320/390px with a long title: no title is squeezed down to 1–2 words per line.
Field & mobile
R-02
Text that carries action information ≥ 14px (field density: 16px). The smallest text in the system is 12px, only for secondary labels. 9–11px is forbidden.Readable in harsh light and at arm’s length (F-21).Verify: Scan the CSS: no font-size < 12px.
R-03
Minimum touch target 44×44px; 48px in field density (primary action button 56px). Spacing between two touch targets ≥ 8px. The whole row is tappable, not just the tick box.Gloves, wet hands, hurried actions (F-07, F-19).Verify: Measure with DevTools; test with real gloves.
R-05
The screen’s primary action sits in the thumb zone (lower half). Do not put frequent actions at the top of the page.One-handed use while the other hand is busy (F-06).Verify: The “Next item”/“Save & continue” button is at the bottom of the screen.
R-06
On mobile, the page’s primary action is a StickyActionBar fixed at the bottom (above the bottom nav), always visible while scrolling; at most 2 buttons.No scrolling up/down to find the button.Verify: Scroll to the end of the page: the button is still at the bottom.
R-07
Checklists: one row = one item (status · name · badge · person/time). Details open on a separate screen/panel, not by expanding 3–4 lines inside the list.Scan 30 items quickly; less scrolling (F-07).Verify: Every row ≤ 72px when collapsed.
R-08
Evidence is camera-first: the capture button opens the camera directly; “Library” is a secondary action. Video compression/upload shows step-by-step progress and a Cancel button.One less step for every photo (F-09).Verify: From a check item to an attached photo in ≤ 2 taps.
R-28
Choose density by context: compact (office data tables) · comfortable (default) · field (QC/stock count on mobile). Density is set at the screen root, not per component.The same component adapts to context instead of being duplicated.Verify: A data-density attribute on the screen root.
Data integrity (most important for QC)
R-10
One save model for every input: autosave 800ms after typing stops (or immediately for tick/select) + an always-visible SaveState. No separate “Submit” button per field any more.Interruptions do not lose data (F-04).Verify: Every field has a Saved / Saving / Could not save indicator.
R-11
Never fail silently: every save/submit ends in one of 3 clear states; a dialog/form does not close until the save succeeds and keeps the entered data.Staff will trust the data was recorded unless the UI says otherwise (F-01).Verify: Cut the network/simulate a 500: the form stays open and shows the error and a Retry button.
R-12
Complete = every required field valid. The “Complete” button/box is locked with a reason (“1 required field left: Hygiene status”) until it is filled. Choosing “Fail” requires entering a corrective action.Prevents “fake completion” in compliance reports (F-02).Verify: Test: leave a * field empty → it cannot be completed.
R-13
Errors speak the user’s language, in one place only (next to the field or an item-level Notice), with how to fix it and an action button. No technical messages leak; technical details go in a collapsed “Details” section.Avoids raw banners and duplicated messages (F-03).Verify: No technical English strings in the UI; one error = one place it is shown.
R-14
Offline: actions go into a local queue, show the state “Waiting for network — will send when connected” and retry automatically; data must never be lost.Cold rooms/basements often lose signal (F-08).Verify: Turn on airplane mode, complete an item, turn it off: the data reaches the server.
R-15
Long tasks (compress/upload) show each step (Compressing → Sending), can be Cancelled, and report the result with a toast + SaveState.Users know what the device is doing (F-09).Verify: No 0–100% progress bar that merges several steps.
Colour, content & formats
R-16
Colour is used only to carry meaning (status, warning, action). No decorative colour on icon tiles or charts outside the data palette.Orange/red always means “attention/error” (F-16).Verify: No colour outside the palette (e.g. purple).
R-17
Status uses a single semantic map (StatusBadge): Default/Draft · Info/Open · In progress (teal) · Success · Warning · Error/Cancelled. Always a dot/icon + text, never colour alone.Same meaning → same look in every module (F-12).Verify: Every status badge goes through one component.
R-18
Rare or destructive actions do not sit next to everyday ones: put them in the “…” menu; delete/post uses a ConfirmDialog that states the consequence (for serious actions: type the name to confirm). Icon-only controls need a tooltip/aria-label.Avoids mis-taps with gloves (F-18).Verify: No red trash icon right next to the Edit button.
R-19
Text contrast ≥ 4.5:1 (large text ≥ 3:1), UI components ≥ 3:1. White text only on navy-500/600, teal-600, green-600, orange-600, red-500+.Readable in poor lighting (F-20).Verify: Run automated contrast checks on the tokens and on screenshots.
R-20
Every system string (labels, buttons, messages, month/day names, onboarding) goes through i18n (VI · EN · KO · ID) with an automated “missing translation keys” check before release. User-generated content (UGC: category/check-item names, instructions, custom field labels, option values) is shown verbatim — there is no translation UI.No more English leaking into the Vietnamese UI (F-11); avoids the burden of translating content that users type themselves.Verify: Switch language: every system label changes; user-entered content stays as typed.
R-21
Number fields have a clear type: numeric keyboard, visible unit (kg, °C, people), accept both “,” and “.” as the decimal separator; errors quote the value the user actually typed and give a valid example.No more “‘1,234’ is unclear” errors (F-05).Verify: Type 1,5 / 1.5 / “abc”: the result and message are correct.
R-27
Numbers use Noto Sans with tabular-nums, right-aligned in tables, always with a unit; large numbers (KPI) 28px/700.Numbers are easier to compare; no font mismatch (F-17).Verify: Number columns line up.
R-29
Date/time is shown in the branch’s time zone and states it when it differs from the viewer’s (“08:12 KST”); formatted by locale.QC time cut-offs show “KST” without explanation.Verify: The time zone appears in the profile and on the Late cut-off.
Feedback & accessibility
R-22
Every control works with the keyboard; focus is always visible (3px navy 28% ring + navy border).Desktop users use the keyboard; automated tests.Verify: Tab through the page: a sensible order and no lost focus.
R-23
Respect prefers-reduced-motion; motion only explains (sheet opens, save done), ≤ 320ms.Reduces fatigue/headaches.Verify: Turn on reduce motion: no animation other than fades.
R-24
Lists load with a Skeleton shaped like the rows, not a full-page spinner.Feels fast and avoids layout jumps.Verify: No “blank page” while loading.
R-25
An empty state always says why it is empty and the next step (primary button), not just “No data”.Guides new users (F-27).Verify: Every list has an Empty state with an action.
R-30
Not enough permission: say which permission is missing and who to contact; hide unusable actions instead of letting people tap and then showing an error.Dynamic permissions (quality_control.manage/execute) are hard to predict.Verify: Sign in as Staff: no admin buttons are visible.

Do
  • A dot/icon + text in the same badge (never rely on colour alone).
  • A 1-line badge, 24px tall, never wrapping.
  • The active state = green, not solid navy.
Don’t
  • Invent a colour for each type (LOSS/DAMAGE/EXPIRE…): use the default badge + a type icon.
  • Use a solid fill with white text for ordinary states — reserve it for states that must stand out (Late, Error).
  • Use colours outside the palette (purple, pink).

Description

A Notice is a message that lives in the page (context, item-level errors). A Toast is a passing confirmation after an action. One event is shown in one place only.

Variants & states
  • Notice: info · success · warning · error; with a title, body and action
  • Toast: 4s, with an Undo button when the action is reversible; not for errors that need an action
Usage rules
  • An error with an action → Notice (not a Toast).
  • No technical strings leak; details live in a collapsed “Details” section (R-13).
Accessibility
  • An error Notice uses role="alert"; a Toast uses role="status" aria-live="polite".

idleNo changes yet
savingSaving…
savedSaved
queuedWaiting for network — will send when connected
errCould not save — retry
Description

A save-state indicator placed right next to the field/block being saved. It is a mandatory component on every autosaving form.

Variants & states
  • idle → saving → saved (held for 3 seconds then fades)
  • queued: offline, placed in the local queue — sent automatically when connected
  • err: with a “Retry” button; the entered data is kept
Usage rules
  • One save model for every input (R-10); no separate “Submit” button per field any more.
  • The overall state at the top of the page (Saved 08:47) aggregates the child fields.
Accessibility
  • aria-live="polite"; errors use role="alert".

Usage rules
  • A Card is only for a standalone object (record, KPI, summary); forms have no boxes and no nested boxes (R-31).
  • Forms are at most 760px wide on desktop; the side column (summary) is a 360px Card on the right.
  • One field per row on mobile; a field with or without help text must not misalign the row (R-32).
  • Short labels and placeholders that always fit the field width.
Accessibility
  • A Section is a section with aria-labelledby pointing at its heading.

The standard list row. It must read well at any width and with long titles: the text always keeps at least ~144px, the trailing element (badge, button, switch) drops under the title when the row is narrow, and the icon tile never squeezes the text. The three frames below are a mandatory test for every row-type component (R-36).

  • RecordRow: title + badge, note, meta line; the whole row is tappable; kebab on the right
Usage rules
  • The text area is always ≥ ~144px (9rem): when there is not enough room the trailing element drops under the title instead of squeezing the text.
  • Titles wrap naturally; codes (SKU, lot number) never break mid-token.
  • Keep the icon tile only when the row is wide enough; on narrow rows drop the icon before squeezing the text.
  • Every row-type component must pass the 3-width × short/long title test before entering the library.

  • The whole row is a link/button; status badges carry text, not colour alone.

Description

The app frame changes shape with width: navy Sidebar (desktop) → icon Rail (tablet) → Topbar + BottomNav (mobile). On mobile, navigation has two tiers: the bottom bar holds the modules; module tabs (under the Topbar) hold the sub-pages of the open module. Page padding 32 → 24 → 16 (card 20 → 16 → 14). Full model in B4 (R-35).

Variants & states
  • BottomNav “General” (users who can reach several modules): Products · Orders · Inventory · QC · More — identical on every screen
  • BottomNav “QC staff” (can reach QC only): Checklist · Calendar · Corrective (badge = open cases) · More — QC’s sub-pages move up to the bottom bar because there is no other module
  • ModuleTabs: underlined tabs that scroll horizontally under the Topbar, only on a module’s root pages (QC · Inventory · Products)
  • Mobile Topbar: (‹ parent name) or the module name · search · notifications · avatar; no menu button; workspace/language go into “More”; the Topbar title never repeats the H1 (R-33)
Usage rules
  • The bottom bar is 64px high + safe-area; the selected item has a navy-50 pill and is always the module that contains the current page (R-35).
  • Deep pages (detail, form, camera) hide ModuleTabs; task pages hide the bottom bar too and keep only the StickyActionBar.
  • The Sidebar keeps the two current groups (Main · Order Plus administration).
Accessibility
  • nav has an aria-label; the current item has aria-current="page"; ModuleTabs use role="tablist".

A QC-specific set of components, optimised for field density: one row per item, a progress ring, category chips, a heatmap calendar and evidence photos with a retention period.

Variants & states
  • ChecklistItem: a 28px round status (not yet · done · issue · skipped) + name + Required tag + person/time
  • ProgressRing: % of required items; colour changes by threshold (≥90 green · ≥60 orange · lower red)
  • Evidence: 72px thumbnail + retention period on each file; the “+” tile is the same size
  • Calendar: green done · orange incomplete · red has issues · grey upcoming
Usage rules
  • A row ≤ 72px when collapsed (R-07); tap the whole row to open the details.
  • Complete only when the required fields are valid (R-12).
  • Every evidence file shows “N days left” (F-09).
Accessibility
  • The state has an icon + text for screen readers: “Completed”, “Failed”.
References
R-07R-12F-06F-07F-29

A StickyActionBar keeps the primary action in the thumb zone; a BulkBar appears when several rows are selected; the Camera view has a 72px capture button.

Variants & states
  • StickyActionBar: at most 2 buttons, always at the bottom of the screen: on task pages it replaces the BottomNav so two bars never stack; upward elev-3 shadow
  • BulkBar: navy-700 background, shown when ≥ 1 row is selected
  • Camera: photo · video · audio, a 72px capture button, the library is secondary
Usage rules
  • On mobile every long form has a StickyActionBar (R-06).
  • Camera-first for evidence (R-08).

B4Layout & interaction patterns

Patterns that combine components into a complete experience. This is where Brand Guidelines currently specify nothing, and it is the source of most P1 findings.

Page templates

TemplateStructureUsed forMobile
ListPageHeader → FilterBar → (Stat) → DataView → paginationOrders, Products, Stores, Users, Stock documentsFilters → sheet; table → rows; primary action full-width
Overview (Dashboard)PageHeader → Stat/Tile → warning Notice → a condensed DataViewInventory overview, QC reportsStat 2×2; warnings first
Detail / FormPageHeader → Sections with headings (no boxes) → StickyActionBarProfile, Create stock document, Check item, Edit itemOne column; a bottom-sticky action bar; SaveState at the top
Execution (Checklist)Progress (ring) → group chips → row list → StickyActionBar “Next item”QC checklist, Stock countField density; tap a row → a full-screen detail page
Configuration / AdministrationPageHeader → Tabs/Segmented → DataView or MatrixQC Manual, Inventory settings, PermissionsMatrix → a role picker + a permission list
Special statesEmpty · No permission · Page error · OfflineEvery templateCentred, one primary action

Mobile navigation model — R-35

Mobile navigation has two tiers and one principle: the bottom bar does not change from screen to screen. Three common mistakes to avoid: a bottom bar whose items change from screen to screen, a “More” that means several things, and screens that belong to no item on the bottom bar. The six rules N1–N6 below remove all three.

#RuleExample
N1Bottom bar = the highest-level destinations the user can reach, identical on every screen (at most 4 modules + “More”).Products · Orders · Inventory · QC · More
N2A module’s sub-pages = ModuleTabs under the Topbar (horizontal scroll); they do not go into the bottom bar.QC: Checklist · Calendar · Corrective · Reports · QC Manual
Inventory: Overview · Stock entry · Stock count · Statistics · Settings
Products: Products for sale · Products to buy · Favourites
N3A user who can reach only one module (QC staff only have execute permission): that module’s sub-pages move up to the bottom bar, since there is no other module to switch to.Checklist · Calendar · Corrective · More
N4The selected item = the module that contains the current page. “More” is a real menu (the “More menu” screen); pages opened from it have a ‹ More button and keep “More” lit.Sellers, Stores, Guide, Profile, Administration → ‹ More button, “More” lit
N5Deep pages (item detail, create receipt, push manual) have a ‹ parent-name button and hide ModuleTabs. Task pages (data entry, camera, create receipt, push manual) hide the bottom bar too and keep only one StickyActionBar so two bars never stack. Only root pages with exactly one primary action (“Daily checklist” → “Next item”, “Stock count” → “Post stock count”) keep that single button right above the bottom bar (not a second bar).Item detail · Create receipt · Push manual
N6There is no “Overview/Home” tab: the system has no global overview page yet; “Inventory overview” is a sub-tab of Inventory.—

Permission → bottom bar: the bar is built from the account’s permissions

#Rule
Q1Permissions decide the bottom bar. The bar is recomputed at sign-in, on workspace change and when permissions change; the desktop Sidebar uses the same filter so the two always match.
Q2Fixed order Products → Orders → Inventory → QC, with “More” always last. Modules without permission are hidden, not greyed out, so people do not tap what they cannot use.
Q3Number of accessible modules: 2 or more → module bar (N1); exactly 1 → promote up to 4 of that module’s sub-pages onto the bar (N3), the rest go into “More”; none → no bar, the home page is the “More” menu.
Q4Sub-items are filtered by permission too: a module tab or bar item only appears if the user can access it (for example “Reports” and “QC Manual” need the manage permission).
Q5Opening the address of a module without permission directly → a “No permission” page inside the app frame (the bottom bar still follows Q1), never a silent redirect.
Q6The “Corrective” count badge follows that item whether it sits on the bar (QC staff) or in a module tab (multi-module users).
Q7At most 4 modules + “More”. If a 5th module is added later, the least-used module moves into “More”.
Needs confirmation before implementationOnly the QC permissions (quality_control.manage and quality_control.execute) are confirmed from the source code. How the Products, Orders and Inventory permissions map to modules, and the example roles in the table above, are proposals. When building, list the existing permissions and the proposed mapping and wait for approval; meanwhile use mock data marked // TODO(data).

Container policy: when to use boxes on mobile — R-34

Flat by default; add a container only when the content needs one (to stand out, to be tappable, to sit on an overlay). Desktop has enough room, so it can keep Cards.

Content typeDesktopMobile (< 768)Why
Record lists (orders, stores, corrective cases…)TableFlat row (RecordRow): a hairline, the whole row tappable, a kebab on the rightDrops 2 borders + padding per row; faster to scan
Checklists (ChecklistItem)A bordered rowFlat row with a 28px status ring30 items/day — every box is an extra scroll
Stat groups (KPI)Stat cardA divided number strip (StatStrip) or 2 flat columns4 cards in 2×2 take ~200px; the strip is only ~70px
Calendars, chartsCardDirectly on the background: a title + a rule, the grid spans the full marginA 7-column calendar gains most: cells ~41 → 46px (+11%)
Forms, detail pagesSectionSection (R-31)Group by heading and spacing
Collapsible groups (accordion, categories)CardFlat rows edge to edgeDrops the side borders
Empty states, photos/thumbnailsCardNo boxNo container needed
Notice / warningA coloured boxA coloured box (kept)Needs to stand out; colour carries meaning
Dialog, Sheet, Menu, ToastFloating shellA floating shell (kept)Sits on an overlay so it needs a container
Quick-action tilesTileTile (kept)It is a button — needs a visible touch area
QC progress bandHero navyA navy band (kept)The shift’s most important number

Save model & error handling

Lifecycle of one save
No changes yetThe user has not edited anything
Saving…800ms after typing stops, or immediately on tick/select
Saved 08:47The server confirms; held for 3 seconds
Waiting for network — will send when connectedOffline: goes into the local queue, retried automatically
Could not save — retryKeep the data; show the reason + a Retry button
Three levels of error messages
  • Field level: the error right under the field + a correct example (R-21).
  • Item/block level: a Notice with a title, how to fix it and an action button (“Fix now”).
  • Page/system level: a top Banner for shared incidents (offline, expired session); technical details collapse into “Details”.

Forbidden: staying silent, closing a dialog before saving, leaking backend strings, reporting the same thing in several places.

Completing a check item (rule R-12)

Before (today)
  • The “Check completed” box and the data fields are separate.
  • It can be ticked even when a * field is empty.
  • Three save behaviours; a separate “Submit” button.
After (v2)
  • The Complete button is enabled only when every required field is valid; if locked → “1 required field left: Hygiene status”.
  • Choosing Fail → a corrective action is required (a corrective case is created automatically).
  • Autosave per field + SaveState; no Submit button.

Special states

Empty

An explanation + a primary action. Filtered to empty → “Clear filters”. First use (QC) → suggested templates.

No permission

“You need the QC Management permission to view this page. Contact your organization’s administrator.” Hide unusable buttons.

Offline

A banner “You are offline — changes are saved on this device and will be sent when the network returns”; SaveState switches to “Waiting for network”.

Loading

A Skeleton shaped like the rows; no full-page spinner; keep the PageHeader frame.

Load error

An error-style Empty: a plain-language cause + a “Reload” button; no raw error code.

Dangerous action

A ConfirmDialog states the consequence; serious deletions require typing the name; posting stock reminds “can only be corrected with an Adjustment document”.

Language, date/time and numbers

TopicRule
Four languagesVI (default) · EN · KO · ID. An i18n key for every string, including the labels/option values of QC custom fields; an automated “missing translation keys” check before release.
User-generated content (UGC)Category/check-item names, instructions, custom-field labels and option values are typed by the user in one language and shown verbatim — there is no translation UI. Only system labels go through i18n.
String lengthDesign for strings up to 40% longer (Vietnamese, Indonesian): do not fix button widths, allow descriptions to wrap onto 2 lines, never wrap badges/codes.
Date & timeBy locale; time states the branch’s time zone when it differs from the viewer’s (“08:12 KST”). The “Late” cut-off is shown with its rule (section A7).
Numbers & currencyTabular-nums; thousands/decimal separators by locale; input accepts both “,” and “.”; the unit is always shown.

B5Tokens as code

The code blocks below are a direct bridge to Lovable/shadcn: paste them as they are into index.css, tailwind.config.ts and the components/ui folder. The HSL values are computed automatically from the exact colours in section B2.

    /* ---- shadcn/ui semantic tokens (HSL triplets: "H S% L%") ---- */
    --background: 0 0% 99%;          /* gray-50  */
    --foreground: 0 0% 18%;          /* gray-800 */
    --card: 0 0% 100%;
    --card-foreground: 0 0% 18%;
    --popover: 0 0% 100%;
    --popover-foreground: 0 0% 18%;
    --primary: 210 100% 31%;             /* navy-500 #0050A0 */
    --primary-foreground: 0 0% 100%;
    --secondary: 217 100% 96%;            /* navy-50  */
    --secondary-foreground: 210 100% 24%;
    --muted: 240 7% 97%;               /* gray-150 */
    --muted-foreground: 223 4% 39%;    /* gray-650 #5F6166 — AA on white & app bg */
    --accent: 217 100% 96%;
    --accent-foreground: 210 100% 16%;
    --destructive: 357 100% 45%;          /* op-red-500 */
    --destructive-foreground: 0 0% 100%;
    --border: 240 6% 91%;
    --input: 240 3% 83%;               /* control border (>= 3:1) */
    --ring: 210 100% 31%;
    --radius: 0.5rem;                            /* md = 8px */

    /* ---- status / flow (v2) ---- */
    --success: 138 100% 24%;   --success-soft: 131 57% 95%;   --success-ink: 139 100% 21%;
    --warning: 21 100% 38%;  --warning-soft: 29 100% 96%;  --warning-ink: 20 100% 33%;
    --danger:  357 100% 45%;     --danger-soft:  0 100% 96%;    --danger-ink:  356 100% 27%;
    --info:    210 100% 31%;    --info-soft:    217 100% 96%;    --info-ink:    210 100% 24%;
    --flow:    177 100% 24%;    --flow-soft:    173 82% 89%;   --flow-ink:    176 100% 16%;

    /* ---- elevation (navy-tint) ---- */
    --elev-1: 0 1px 4px rgba(0,30,90,.08), 0 0 1px rgba(0,30,90,.06);
    --elev-2: 0 2px 8px rgba(0,30,90,.10), 0 1px 2px rgba(0,30,90,.06);
    --elev-3: 0 4px 14px rgba(0,30,90,.12), 0 2px 4px rgba(0,30,90,.06);
    --elev-4: 0 10px 24px rgba(0,30,90,.14), 0 4px 8px rgba(0,30,90,.06);

    /* ---- density (default = comfortable) ---- */
    --ctl-h: 40px;  --row-h: 48px;  --fs: 15px;  --fs-sm: 14px;  --fs-xs: 12px;
    --page-pad: 16px;

    /* ---- motion ---- */
    --dur-fast: 120ms;  --dur-base: 200ms;  --dur-slow: 320ms;
    --ease: cubic-bezier(.2, 0, 0, 1);

  [data-density="compact"] { --ctl-h: 32px; --row-h: 36px; --fs: 14px; --fs-sm: 13px; }
  [data-density="field"]   { --ctl-h: 48px; --row-h: 64px; --fs: 16px; --fs-sm: 15px; }
  @media (min-width: 768px)  { :root { --page-pad: 24px; } }
  @media (min-width: 1024px) { :root { --page-pad: 32px; } }

  html { font-family: 'Noto Sans', 'Noto Sans KR', system-ui, sans-serif; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; -webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased; }
  code, kbd, .font-mono { font-family: 'IBM Plex Mono', ui-monospace, Menlo, monospace; }
  @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { *, *::before, *::after { animation-duration: .01ms !important; transition-duration: .01ms !important; } }
  :focus-visible { outline: 3px solid hsl(var(--ring) / .28); outline-offset: 1px; }
}

// hooks/use-autosave.ts — one save model for every input (R-10, R-11, R-14)
export type SaveState = 'idle' | 'saving' | 'saved' | 'queued' | 'error';
// useAutosave({ value, save, delay = 800 }) →
//   { state, lastSavedAt, retry }
// - debounce 'delay' ms after the last keystroke; tick/select saves immediately
// - navigator.onLine === false  → state = 'queued', write to IndexedDB, send automatically on 'online'
// - server error → state = 'error', KEEP the user's entered value, show a Retry button
// - state 'saved' held for 3s then back to 'idle' (only show the last-saved time)
// - NEVER close a dialog/form while state !== 'saved'

Part C

New UI built from Design System v2

35 screens, each with a desktop and a mobile version, placed next to the current state for comparison.

C0How to read the mockups

35 screens, 33 desktop versions and 35 mobile versions. Every screen has the same layout so they are easy to compare.

Desktop 1440px

A large frame; switch between New design and Current (real screenshot) with the toggle right above the frame.

Mobile 390px

The left column is the real current mobile screenshot (606px), the middle column is the new design at 390px — comparing like devices, never desktop against mobile.

Sample data

The data comes from the workspace “tested”: branch Alexidntest, 5 QC categories/30 items, the real organizations. The data is only illustrative, not real figures.

A note about the new designsThe new designs in this document (Part C and the samples in Part B) are a directional reference for UX/UI, not a final specification. Some details may not be exactly right — layout, sizes, sample content, on-screen text, behaviour. Real implementation may differ, and will be more accurate after testing with real users, real data and technical constraints. When a mockup conflicts with an R-xx rule or with real data, prefer the rule and the data, then note the difference.

The mockups are static HTML/CSS generated from Design System v2, so tapping the buttons does nothing; behaviour (autosave, offline queue, confirmation) is described in B4 and in the D2 acceptance criteria.

Goal
  • Branch staff complete the shift checklist quickly and correctly, and know what's left.
Key changes
  • Structure change: from "big hero + filters + list" to a progress cluster (% ring + required-item count) → category chips → list; everything actionable sits in the thumb zone.
  • Each item is one row: a 28px status circle, name, Required badge, who + when. No more 3–4-line rows with a checkbox and a history button.
  • The "Next item" button is sticky at the bottom of the screen (mobile) and always visible in the right panel (desktop).
  • Desktop 2 columns: one panel merging shift summary + categories (categories scroll on their own, not with the summary) | list (the open item expands right there). Mobile: tapping a row opens the full-screen detail view.
  • Complete = all required fields are valid (no more a separate "done" tick apart from the input).

Goal
  • Record one check item accurately — data, evidence, corrective action — with no possibility of “fake completion”.
Key changes
  • One single save model: autosave per field + an always-visible state (“Saved 08:47” / “Could not save”); the 3 mixed save behaviours (instant tick, blur, Submit button) are removed.
  • The Complete button is enabled only when every required field is valid; choosing “Fail” requires entering a Corrective action (fixes completing while a * field is empty).
  • Number fields use a stepper/numeric keyboard with a unit — no more “‘1,234’ is unclear” errors; on mobile the stepper is full-width with the − + buttons at both ends.
  • The content is split into titled Sections (Instructions · Record · Evidence) instead of nested boxes, so input fields span almost the whole screen width.
  • Taking a photo is the primary action (it opens the camera directly), the library is secondary; every photo shows its retention “31 days left”.
  • The completion history collapses inside an accordion.

Goal
  • HQ sets the inspection standard once and pushes it to branches in a controlled way.
Key changes
  • Keep the “Standard manual → push to branches” model (a good point) but turn the scope banner into a clear action bar with a “Push down” button sticky at the top.
  • The configuration error currently shows verbatim technical text (“a field needs one name stored as written”) → a readable item-level message + a “Fix now” button, technical details collapsed.
  • Categories as an accordion; each item is a row with the name spanning the full width and the badge/time on the line below, drag handles only on desktop (mobile: a “Reorder” button), edit/delete in the “…” menu.
  • The stats 5 categories / 30 items / 23 required collapse into one meta line instead of 3 big cards.

Goal
  • Create a check item with custom data fields, without producing configuration errors.
Key changes
  • The item name and instructions are typed in one language (the branch’s language): this is user-generated content so it is shown verbatim, with no translation tabs — multi-language only applies to system labels.
  • Custom fields have clear types (Pick one, Number + unit, Text, Photo) and are marked required; the Number type carries a note “enter a quantity” so staff do not type a name.
  • Mobile: a full-height bottom sheet with a sticky action bar; desktop: a 560px dialog.
  • A fixed note: the Checkbox is always present; photo/video is additional evidence.

Goal
  • Fixes the P0 bug: saving a category fails silently (reproduced 2 out of 2 times on production).
Key changes
  • Never close the dialog before saving succeeds: a missing name → an error right under the field; a server error/lost connection → a readable Notice with a “Retry” button, and the dialog keeps the entered data (shown: the error state).
  • On success → the dialog closes, a toast “Category created” with the hint “Push to branches when ready”, and the category count is updated.
  • The Save button shows a saving state (spinner) to prevent repeat taps.

  • After pushing: a confirmation toast; shifts already in progress at a branch are not changed midway (a warning is shown).

Goal
  • A manager of several branches switches context in 2 taps and sees which branch needs attention.
Key changes
  • A bottom sheet (mobile) / popover (desktop) with a search field, a “Favourites” group and an “All” group.
  • Each branch shows today’s completion % as a coloured ring (green ≥90%, orange ≥60%, red lower) — you see at a glance which branch is falling behind.
  • Remembers the last branch for the next time it is opened.

Staff health & hygiene
Waiting for network · 2 photos will be sent automatically
PHOTOVIDEOAUDIO
Tap to capture · auto-compressed before sending
Goal
  • Capture photo/video/audio evidence quickly with one hand, even wearing gloves, in the kitchen/warehouse.
Key changes
  • The camera is the primary action and opens the viewfinder directly instead of a file-picker box (Photo library / Take photo / File).
  • Switch between photo · video · audio with the bottom tabs, a 72px capture button in the thumb zone; video is auto-compressed to 720p with step-by-step progress “Compressing” / “Sending” and a Cancel button.
  • Offline: photos go into the local queue (a “Waiting for network” badge) and are sent automatically when connected.
  • Desktop: replaced by a drag-and-drop area + a “Choose photos” button (no camera needed).
Components used
Camera viewSegmented tabsIconButtonSaveState (queued)

  • The “Current stock” table becomes item rows on mobile.

Goal
  • Compose an accurate receipt with few quantity errors, even when entering on a phone in the warehouse.
Key changes
  • From a cramped dialog to a separate page with a sticky action bar: “Save draft” | “Post”.
  • The form is split into two titled Sections (Document information · Line items), with no box around each group; on mobile each field takes its own row so labels and placeholders always fit.
  • Quantities are entered with the standard QuantityInput (comma becomes a dot; numeric keyboard) + a full-width stepper on mobile — no more “1,234” entry errors.
  • Line items are rows separated by rules (name, code, UoM, on hand) rather than cards nested in cards.
  • A warning before Post: the action updates stock and can only be corrected with an Adjustment document.

Getting started

Getting started

The SCM app supports multiple organizations. All operating data lives in one Workspace, belonging to one Organization. Choose the right context before you work.

Getting startedThe SCM app supports multiple organizations. All operating data lives in one Workspace, belonging to one Organization. Choose the right context before you work.

Daily operations

Order management

View and analyse OrderPlus orders of the stores registered in the current workspace.

Sellers & Suppliers

Register OrderPlus sellers into the current workspace. Each seller has a version history and brings its own product catalogue.

Store management

A franchise store is a real point of sale you serve. The store type determines the Inbound and Outbound flow.

Product management

Browse the seller and supplier catalogues imported into the workspace, and manage favourites per branch.

Inventory

Inventory overview

A dashboard summarising stock status and quick actions.

Items & Warehouses

The master data underlying every transaction. Items and warehouses are unique within a workspace.

Stock entry

Inbound, Outbound, Transfer and Adjustment all follow the DRAFT → POSTED workflow.

Stock count

Reconcile system quantities with the physical count. Variance is generated automatically.

Reports

Ten reports on transactions and stock, exportable to Excel.

Warehouse settings

The catalogue of items, warehouses, units of measure and stock-alert thresholds.

  • Localise the article names “Sellers & Suppliers” and “Item & Kho”; no new data is added (no reading time, no role labels).

Part D

Hand-off to Lovable

How to use it, the phase-by-phase prompt pack, the screen map, acceptance and open questions.

D1How to use this document with Lovable

The document is structured to serve as direct input for a draft on Lovable: Part B supplies tokens and components as code, Part C supplies mockups (desktop + mobile) as reference images, and Part D supplies phase-by-phase prompts together with acceptance criteria.

Before you start
  1. Identify the real code source. The Lovable project orderplusscm is older than production (F-33). Take the Vercel repo/branch that is actually deployed and import it into Lovable (or sync via GitHub) before applying anything.
  2. Create a new project/separate branch for the draft — do not edit production directly.
  3. Paste the Project Knowledge block below into the project’s Knowledge section.
  4. Export the Part C screen images to attach in advance (each phase lists which).
Working principles
  • Run P0 → P7 in order, one pass per phase (or split by screen); do not send “rebuild the whole system” in one go.
  • After each phase: check against that phase’s acceptance criteria before moving on.
  • Prompts are written in English so that Lovable understands them precisely; UI strings still follow i18n (VI · EN · KO · ID).
  • Wherever you see [PASTE: …], it is a code block taken verbatim from section B5.
  • The Part C mockups are a directional reference, not a pixel-level spec: when they conflict with an R-xx rule or real data, the rule/data wins and the difference should be noted.
  • Every Lovable turn consumes credits — group by phase rather than sending many small messages.
Project Knowledge — paste into Lovable (Settings → Knowledge)
# OrderPlus SQM — Design System v2 (Project Knowledge)
Product: Supply & Quality Manager for restaurant/franchise operations. Users: QC staff on phones in kitchens/warehouses (gloves, glare, weak network), branch managers (phone+tablet), HQ/QA and admins (desktop).
Stack: React + Vite + TypeScript + Tailwind + shadcn/ui + Supabase. Keep business logic, routes, RLS and RPCs unchanged unless a task says otherwise.
Languages: vi (default), en, ko, id — every UI string goes through i18n; never hard-code text.

Non-negotiables (see blueprint Part B1 for R-xx ids):
- Brand: navy-500 #0050A0 primary, teal for "flow/in-progress", op-red #E8000C for danger. Font: Noto Sans (+ Noto Sans KR), IBM Plex Mono for codes. No purple/other hues.
- One PageHeader on every page. One FilterBar. Tables become record cards below 768px (container query), never horizontal scroll on mobile.
- Density: data-density = compact | comfortable | field. QC + count screens on mobile use "field" (controls 48px, primary action 56px, text >= 16px body / 14px min).
- Touch targets >= 44px (48px in field). Text never below 12px. WCAG AA contrast: white text only on navy-500/600, teal-600, green-600, orange-600, red-500+.
- ONE save model: autosave (debounce 800ms; immediate for tick/select) + <SaveState/> (idle|saving|saved|queued|error). Never silently fail; never close a dialog before the save succeeded; keep user input on error and show "Retry".
- A checklist item is complete only when ALL required fields are valid; otherwise the Complete button is disabled with a reason. "Fail" requires a corrective action.
- Status colours come from ONE map (<StatusBadge status="..."/>): neutral, info, flow(teal), success, warning, danger. Always dot/icon + text.
- Destructive/rare actions live in the "..." menu and require <ConfirmDialog/> that states the consequence.
- Dialog >= 768px, BottomSheet < 768px. Primary action on mobile is a StickyActionBar that replaces the BottomNav on task pages (never stack two bars).
- Data: elements marked "Needs new/changed data" or "Needs confirmation" in blueprint D3 need backend changes. Do NOT silently add tables/columns/RPCs: list the proposed schema changes first and wait for approval; meanwhile build the UI against mock data marked // TODO(data).
- Mobile content is FLAT by default: lists are hairline-divided rows (no bordered box per row), stat groups are a single divided strip, calendars/charts/forms sit directly on the page. Boxes are only for things that need a container: Notice, Dialog/Sheet, tappable tiles, the QC progress band. Desktop may keep cards.
- The blueprint mockups are DIRECTIONAL references, not pixel-perfect specs: some details (layout, sizes, sample content, copy, behaviour) may be imperfect and real implementation may differ and end up more accurate. When a mockup conflicts with a rule (R-xx), real data, or a technical constraint, follow the rule/data and note the difference in your summary.
- Numbers: tabular-nums, units always shown, accept "," and "." decimals.
- i18n covers SYSTEM strings only. User-generated content (checklist/category/item names, instructions, custom-field labels and option values) is single-language and shown verbatim — never build translation UI for it.
- Forms and detail pages use <FormSection/> (heading + spacing + hairline divider), NOT cards around each group; cards are for standalone objects (records, KPIs, summaries). Never nest cards. Mobile form fields are one per row (<FormGrid/>), paired only for short values.
- Exactly ONE back affordance: on mobile it is the Topbar chevron labelled with the parent name; PageHeader never repeats it. Topbar title = section name (root pages) or parent name (sub-pages), never the H1 again. Mobile page gutter 16px, card padding 14px.
Nothing has been sent to Lovable yetAs requested, this document is finalised before it goes to Lovable. Creating the draft, reading/writing the project and deploying happen only after you have reviewed the document.
QC can run on several pages at onceThis update is mostly UX/UI, data barely changes (see D3) — spots needing data changes are already flagged clearly. So QC can check multiple pages at once instead of page by page; just look closer at the “Needs new/changed data” or “Needs confirmation” items.
Pending decision: run v1/v2 side by side, or ship straight?Production currently has only 1 real customer (TOPAS), the rest are test workspaces, so staging the rollout by workspace doesn’t mean much. Two options on the table: (a) a feature flag per page, v1/v2 running side by side; (b) build the whole thing on Lovable, QC it, then ship straight to TOPAS at a coordinated time, keeping a fast rollback path. Not decided yet — checking back with whoever proposed it on what the real concern is before choosing.

D2Phase-by-phase prompt pack (P0 → P7)

Eight phases going from foundations to quality. P0–P2 are prerequisites (tokens, shell, shared patterns); P3 (QC) has the highest priority because it contains the three P0 bugs and serves the field users.

PhaseScopeDepends onRisk if skipped
P0Foundations—Everything after it drifts off-standard, contrast fails
P1Shell & navigationP0Mobile has no BottomNav; page headers stay in 5 styles
P2Shared patternsP0, P1Each module rebuilds its own table/filter/dialog
P3Quality ControlP0–P2The three P0 bugs remain; QC on mobile is still unusable
P4InventoryP0–P2Stock count/goods receipt remain hard to use on a phone
P5Remaining listsP0–P2Inconsistent across pages
P6Authentication · Administration · i18nP0–P2English still leaks into the UI
P7Quality & accessibilityP0–P6No assurance for the R-xx rules
P0

Foundations: tokens, fonts, density, primitives

Bring every v2 token into the code, change the font, add density, restyle the shadcn primitives — without changing page layouts yet.

Attachments / references

Sections B2, B5 (3 code blocks), B3 (Button, Input, Choice, Badge, Card, Notice, Save)

Prompt P0
Read Project Knowledge first. This step changes ONLY the design foundations, no page layouts, routes or business logic.

1. In index.html remove the Spoqa Han Sans Neo <link>. In src/index.css replace the token block with the one below and load Noto Sans, Noto Sans KR and IBM Plex Mono.
[PASTE: blueprint B5 · block 1 (index.css)]
2. Extend tailwind.config.ts with:
[PASTE: blueprint B5 · block 2 (tailwind.config.ts)]
3. Add a <DensityProvider density="compact|comfortable|field"> that sets data-density on the app root; default comfortable. Export useDensity().
4. Restyle the shadcn primitives to match blueprint B3 (Button: variants primary/secondary/outline/ghost/teal/danger/danger-outline and sizes sm 32/md 40/lg 48/field 56 driven by --ctl-h; Input/Select/Textarea: white bg, border-input, 3px ring on focus, error state; Checkbox 20px (28px in field) with row-wide hit area; Switch on = teal-600; Card: border + shadow-elev-1, no gradient hero; Tabs: underline; Segmented: new component; Badge: 24px height, dot, never wraps).
5. Create components/ui/status-badge.tsx from:
[PASTE: blueprint B5 · block 3 (status-badge)]
and replace every ad-hoc status colour class in the app with <StatusBadge status="..."/> (Users "active", Inventory DRAFT/POSTED/CANCELLED, Transfer cancelled, Adjustment types, Sellers sync, Franchise "HQ-owned"). Adjustment types use a neutral badge + icon.
6. Create ui/save-state.tsx, ui/notice.tsx (info/success/warning/error + optional action), ui/empty-state.tsx, ui/skeleton-rows.tsx, ui/confirm-dialog.tsx.
7. Download the 4 official logo SVGs into /public/brand and stop hotlinking them from orderplus-sqm-bg.lovable.app.
8. Search the code for text-[9px], text-[10px], text-[11px] and raise all to at least text-xs (12px); replace shadow-sm/md with shadow-elev-1..4.

Acceptance criteria

  • No more Spoqa; the font renders as Noto Sans (DevTools).
  • No more font-size < 12px and no more shadow-sm/md.
  • Token contrast meets the A6 table (white text only on v2 fills).
  • One StatusBadge replaces every status badge; no more purple/emerald.
  • The app still runs as before (no flow/route changes).
P1

App shell & navigation

Sidebar/Rail/BottomNav + Topbar v2 + a shared PageHeader.

Attachments / references

Section B3 (AppShell, PageHeader), Part C: any 3 screens (desktop + mobile)

Prompt P1
Implement the responsive app shell from blueprint B3 "AppShell" using CSS container queries.
- >= 1024px: existing navy Sidebar (264px, two groups: "Main" / "Order Plus administration") + Topbar (search ⌘K, workspace switcher, language, notifications, avatar).
- 768–1023px: 72px icon Rail + Topbar.
- < 768px: Topbar (back "‹ parent name" on sub-pages, otherwise the section name · search · notifications · avatar) + BottomNav. Mobile navigation has TWO tiers and the BottomNav is IDENTICAL on every screen (blueprint rule R-35): BottomNav = top-level destinations the user can reach: Products · Orders · Inventory · QC · More (max 4 modules + More). The sub-pages of a module are ModuleTabs under the Topbar (horizontal scroll, only on the module's root pages): QC = Checklist · Calendar · Corrective · Reports · QC Manual; Inventory = Overview · Stock entry · Stock count · Statistics · Settings; Products = Products for sale · Products to buy · Favourites. Exception: a user whose only accessible module is QC (staff role) gets the QC sub-pages on the BottomNav instead: Checklist · Calendar · Corrective (badge = number of open corrective actions) · More. The highlighted item is always the module that contains the current page; "More" is a real menu screen (user card, Switch workspace, Catalogues & reference: Sellers/Stores/Guide, Order Plus administration (admins only), Account) and highlights only for pages inside it. Pages opened from "More" (Sellers, Stores, Guide, Profile, Administration) show "‹ More" as their back button. There is NO "Overview" tab because there is no global overview page. Deep pages (item detail, create receipt, push manual) show "‹ parent" and no ModuleTabs; task pages (data entry, camera, create receipt, push manual) hide the BottomNav and keep only the StickyActionBar; root pages with exactly one primary action ("Daily checklist" → "Next item", "Stock count" → "Post stock count") keep that single button directly above the BottomNav (a button, not a second bar). Workspace switcher and language live in "More".
- The BottomNav is PERMISSION-DRIVEN (blueprint B4 "Permission → bottom bar", rules Q1–Q7): build it from the modules the account can access, in the fixed order Products → Orders → Inventory → QC, with "More" always last; hide modules without permission (never grey them out) and recompute on login, workspace change and permission change; the desktop Sidebar uses the same filter. 2+ accessible modules → module bar (e.g. Inventory · QC · More); exactly 1 module → promote up to 4 of its sub-pages (QC execute-only: Checklist · Calendar · Corrective · More; QC manage: Checklist · Calendar · Corrective · Reports · More, with "QC Manual" moved into "More"; Inventory only: Overview · Stock entry · Stock count · Statistics · More; Products only: Products for sale · Products to buy · Favourites · More); no accessible module → no bar, home = the "More" menu. Sub-pages are filtered by permission too. Opening a URL without permission shows a "No permission" page inside the shell. Only the QC permissions (quality_control.manage / execute) are confirmed; the mapping of the other modules to permissions is a proposal: list the existing permissions and your proposed mapping first and wait for approval (// TODO(data)).
- Page padding 16 / 24 / 32 px (replace the fixed p-6).
- Create <PageHeader crumb title description meta actions/> and use it on EVERY page (delete the 5 existing header variants). No workspace chip and no "Back" link inside the page header: on mobile the Topbar shows the single back chevron with the parent name on sub-pages, otherwise the section name; there is no hamburger button (the BottomNav "More" tab opens the full menu).
- List rows (ListItem, RecordRow, ChecklistItem) must survive long text and narrow containers (rule R-36): text area >= 9rem, trailing badge/button/switch wraps UNDER the title when there is not enough room, ids/SKUs never break mid-token, icon tile is dropped before squeezing text. Test each row component at 260 / 320 / 390px with a 50-character title before shipping.
- Support safe-area insets for BottomNav and StickyActionBar.

Acceptance criteria

  • At 390px there is no horizontal scroll; the BottomNav is identical on every screen (except task pages) and a module's sub-pages appear in ModuleTabs.
  • Every page uses the PageHeader (no more gradient hero/icon tile/workspace chip).
  • Going 390 → 800 → 1280px does not break the layout or flicker on resize.
P2

Shared patterns: DataView, FilterBar, ResponsiveDialog, autosave

Ready-made building blocks so the modules can just use them.

Attachments / references

Section B3 (DataView, FilterBar, Overlay, SaveState, Stepper), B4

Prompt P2
Create shared patterns (no page rewrites yet):
1. <DataView columns rows card /> — renders a table when its container is >= 768px and FLAT record rows below (hairline-divided, no bordered box per row; whole row tappable; container query, not window width). Column roles: title, subtitle, badge, numeric (right aligned, tabular), meta. Row actions: primary action + "…" menu (menu becomes a BottomSheet on mobile). Codes such as SKU-001 never wrap.
2. <FilterBar search filters chips /> — 1 search + up to 3 inline filters on desktop; on mobile a "Filters (n)" button opening <FilterSheet/> (BottomSheet) and removable chips for active filters.
3. <ResponsiveDialog/> — Dialog (max 560px) >= 768px, BottomSheet < 768px, same children; footer actions stick to the bottom on mobile. It must NOT close while an async save is pending or failed.
4. useAutosave({ value, save, delay: 800 }) + <SaveState state/> per the spec in blueprint B5 block 4: debounce, immediate for tick/select, 'queued' when offline (IndexedDB) with automatic retry on 'online', 'error' keeps the user's input and exposes retry().
5. <QuantityInput unit min max step/> — inputmode="decimal", accepts "," and ".", stepper buttons (56px in field density), error message quotes the value the user typed and gives a valid example.
6. <StickyActionBar/> (max 2 buttons, replaces BottomNav on task pages), <BulkBar/> and <StatStrip items/> (several numbers in one hairline-divided row, no boxes).
7. <FormSection title description actions/> (heading + spacing, hairline divider between sections, no card) and <FormGrid/> (2 columns on desktop, 1 column below 768px, "keep" variant for short pairs). Form pages are max-width 760px on desktop.
Add unit tests for useAutosave (debounce, offline queue, error keeps input) and QuantityInput parsing (1,5 / 1.5 / abc).

Acceptance criteria

  • DataView switches table ↔ rows with the container width (including inside a Drawer).
  • ResponsiveDialog does not close when saving fails; the entered data is kept.
  • useAutosave has tests for debounce, the offline queue and errors.
  • QuantityInput accepts 1,5 and 1.5; errors quote the value actually typed.
P3

Quality Control module

Apply every new pattern to QC and fix the 3 P0 bugs (F-01, F-02, F-03).

Attachments / references

Part C: qc-checklists, qc-item, qc-evidence, qc-calendar, qc-corrective, qc-reports, qc-manuals, qc-item-editor, qc-add-category, qc-push, qc-branch, qc-empty (desktop + mobile)

Prompt P3
Rebuild the Quality Control module screens to match the attached mockups (blueprint Part C: qc-*). Keep the data model, RPCs (qc_get_or_create_records, qc_calendar_summary), snapshots, evidence bucket and permissions (quality_control.manage / execute) unchanged.

Behavioural requirements (bug fixes first):
A. [F-01] "Add category" dialog must never close before the insert succeeded. On error keep the dialog open, keep the input, show a human-readable message and a Retry button. On success show a toast and refetch counts.
B. [F-02] A checklist item is complete only when every required custom field is valid. Replace the separate "Check completed" checkbox + per-field "Submit" button with: autosave per field (useAutosave) + a Complete button that is disabled with the reason "N required fields left: …". Selecting "Fail" requires a corrective action note.
C. [F-03] Never render backend error strings. Map config errors (e.g. "a field needs one name stored as written") to an item-level <Notice> with a "Fix now" action; put the raw text inside a collapsed "Details". One error → one place (no duplicate toast).
D. Custom fields have clear types (select / number with unit / short text / photo). Number fields use <QuantityInput/> with a unit. Field labels, select values, item names and instructions are user-generated content in ONE language chosen by the manager: render them verbatim, no translation UI, no language tabs.

Screens:
1. qc-checklists — density="field" on mobile. Progress ring (required items) → category chips → one row per item (status circle 28px, title, Required tag, who/when) → StickyActionBar "Next item". Desktop: 3 columns (categories | list with the open item expanded inline | shift summary). Tapping a row on mobile opens qc-item full screen.
2. qc-item — fields with SaveState, evidence thumbnails with "N days left" retention, history in an accordion, Complete button per rule B.
3. qc-evidence — camera-first (getUserMedia / <input capture="environment">), photo·video·audio tabs, 72px shutter, video compression with separate "Compressing / Sending" steps and Cancel, offline queue badge "Waiting for network".
4. qc-calendar — cells >= 44px, text >= 14px, month label localized, tap day → detail card.
5. qc-corrective — cross-branch list, default filter "Open", card per case, badge count on the "Corrective" tab (QC ModuleTab; on the BottomNav for QC-only staff). Cases close only after a passing re-check (existing rule).
6. qc-reports — NEW screen: week/month segmented, completion rate, violations, average resolution time, trend line, by-category bars, top repeated issues, branch filter, export. Use existing data; add a Supabase view/RPC only if needed and list it in your summary.
7. qc-manuals, qc-item-editor, qc-add-category, qc-push (diff before pushing: added/changed/removed items, branch selection with last-push date, "Push to N branches"), qc-branch (BottomSheet with search, favorites, completion ring per branch), qc-empty (starter templates).
Explain "Late" (late) with a tooltip/sheet showing the rule (opening after 11:00, mid-day after 15:00, custom = time + 2h).

Acceptance criteria

  • Create a category with a simulated 500: the dialog stays open and shows the error + Retry.
  • Leave a * field empty → the Complete button is locked with a reason; choosing “Fail” requires a corrective action.
  • No more technical English strings; one error is shown in one place only.
  • Turn on airplane mode, complete an item: “Waiting for network” appears; turn it off and the data reaches the server.
  • Mobile 390px: the first check item is visible on the first screen; touch targets ≥ 48px; the “Next item” button is bottom-sticky.

D5General acceptance criteria

Every phase has its own criteria (D2). The list below applies to the whole draft before it is put in front of real users.

Function & data
  • No change to business flows, routes, RLS or RPCs without a separate request.
  • The 3 P0 bugs (F-01, F-02, F-03) are fixed and tested.
  • Every autosaving form shows a SaveState; no dialog closes before saving finishes.
  • Offline: QC actions enter a queue and sync when the network returns.
Interface & consistency
  • One PageHeader, one FilterBar, one DataView and one StatusBadge across the whole system.
  • No horizontally scrolling tables at 390px; text ≥ 12px; touch targets ≥ 44px (48px in field density).
  • No colours outside the palette; shadows use only elev-1..4.
Accessibility & language
  • axe-core: 0 critical errors at 390px and 1440px.
  • Text contrast ≥ 4.5:1; visible focus; operable by keyboard.
  • VI · EN · KO · ID complete; CI fails on a missing i18n key.
Performance & devices
  • Test on a mid-range phone (an Android 2–3 years old) and an iPhone SE.
  • Test with real gloves in a simulated kitchen/warehouse environment (harsh light, wet hands).
  • Video compression does not overheat the phone or freeze the UI; there is a Cancel button.

Measuring success (proposed)

MetricHow to measureSuggested target
Time to complete a shift checklist (30 items)A session with real QC staffLower than today (measure a baseline first)
Number of scrolls to reach the next itemObservation/recording≤ 1 tap (“Next item”)
Share of items completed but missing a required fieldA data query0%
Number of failed saves with no messageLogs + testing0
Number of untranslated strings found in the UIScript i18n CI0

D6Open questions & assumptions

Points the product/engineering team needs to confirm before or during implementation. Each point states the assumption used in the design.

#QuestionAssumption in the designImpact if wrong
Q1Which Vercel repo/branch is deployed? The Lovable code orderplusscm is older than production (F-33).Use production as the standard; use Lovable only as a reference for the data model.P0–P3 may have to be redone on a different codebase.
Q2Does the backend have an offline/queue mechanism for QC (F-08)?A client-side queue (IndexedDB) will be built + syncing when the network returns.An idempotent API is needed to avoid duplicate writes on resend.
Q3Does user-generated content (category/item names, instructions, field labels) need multi-language translation?No (decided): shown verbatim; i18n only applies to system labels.—
Q4Does “complete = required fields valid” change historical reports (R-12)?It applies to new data; old data keeps its snapshot.Old compliance figures may be re-evaluated.
Q5For the new “QC Report” screen: is the weekly/monthly data and average resolution time already available in qc_checklist_records + corrective actions?There is enough data; if not, an aggregate view/RPC will be added.A migration and performance testing are needed.
